uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. It is the figure the Bank of England's 2% target is judged against, and gilts, sterling and mortgage pricing move with it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics publishes the UK's September consumer price reading, which settles how fast prices rose over the month and where UK inflation stood as the summer ended.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. It is the price of dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt are indexed to it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee raised rates 12-0 on September 16 because a closed strait pushed oil into US consumer prices, which rose 0.4% in August. Tightening into a supply shock is a choice it must make again with the strait still closed, and this time without the unanimity a first move buys. Trump has publicly called for lower rates.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets one policy rate for the 20 countries sharing the euro. It meets eight times a year, and its decisions set the cost of borrowing for some 350 million people across very different economies.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The argument in Frankfurt is no longer the size of the energy shock but whether it is passing through: Brent near $110 a barrel after a closed strait has turned a supply price into a second-round transmission question, and Deutsche Bank has already lifted its expected ECB peak to 2.75%.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which sets Japan's short-term interest rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. Because Japanese savings fund borrowing worldwide, what it decides moves the yen and the cost of money far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Japan raised rates in September to curb rising prices, and what is unsettled now is the currency rather than the price level: officials have weighed steering the yen with pension money instead, and the balancing act with Bessent is the constraint on doing it. This meeting tests whether Tokyo keeps tightening while Washington is tightening too.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, whose nine members vote individually on Bank Rate about eight times a year. It sets what British banks pay for reserves, and feeds through to mortgages, business lending and the pound.
boe-2026-11.recent: Brent settled near $106 a barrel this month, an imported cost no rate decision can reach — and other central banks have already moved on it: the Fed raised in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the Bank of Japan to 1.25%, a 31-year high. What this meeting settles is whether the households exposed to it pay for that supply shock twice.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, so borrowing costs from US mortgages to emerging-market debt move with it.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee raised rates 12-0 in September, tightening into a supply shock rather than a demand boom: Brent above $100 after the closure of a strait pushed August consumer prices up 0.4%. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call before that vote, and the December meeting settles whether a war-driven price level is something this committee keeps chasing.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual summit of the Group of Twenty: 19 major economies, the EU and the African Union, which together produce most of the world's output. The rotating host sets the agenda, and the communiqué shows where they agree on trade, debt and finance.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Zelensky has said he is ready to meet Putin face-to-face at the G20 in Miami, which would bring the war to a US-hosted table while Russian strikes on Odesa continue. It follows a BRICS summit where Xi took centre stage and members pushed for payment mechanisms that side-step the US dollar, a rival club courting the same capitals.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets one policy rate for every country sharing the euro. Its deposit rate anchors bank funding across a currency union of twenty-odd economies with no common budget.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Brent has sat near $110 a barrel since the Bab el-Mandeb disruption, and Deutsche Bank has already lifted its ECB peak to 2.75% — a bet that Frankfurt treats the energy shock as having passed into wages and services rather than as a one-off. This decision settles which reading the Council holds, for borrowers across the union who pay either way.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate — the floor under British mortgages, savings returns and government borrowing costs. Sterling and the gilt market move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Fed raised rates 12-0 into a supply shock and the Bank of Japan went to a 31-year high, both tightening against oil near $106 a barrel rather than against domestic demand. The committee meets into that same imported shock, and what it settles is how much of the cost lands on borrowers.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank sets the short-term policy rate and steers the yield curve for the world's largest creditor nation. Its decisions ripple outward through Japanese savings parked abroad, and the yen moves against every major currency with them.
boj-2026-12.recent: The Bank has already moved: it raised its rate to a 31-year high in September to curb rising prices, ending decades of cheap money at home. December settles whether that was a single correction or the start of a run, at a moment when Tokyo is weighing whether to steer the yen using pension money rather than rates alone — and when the Fed's own hike, delivered unanimously, has left the gap between the two central banks the thing the currency turns on.

fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly measure of US output, published as an advance estimate and then revised twice as fuller data arrives. It sets the baseline for Federal Reserve policy, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.recent: This release settles how fast the US economy grew in a quarter that has already ended, using revised figures built on fuller source data. Nothing in recent reporting sets this reading apart from a routine one. Later arguments about the pace of US growth will start from this number.

fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal consumption expenditures — what Americans earn, what they spend, and what they pay for it. Its price index is the gauge the Federal Reserve targets, and the one policy is written against.
fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes the next reading on 30 September, covering the month just closed. It will settle what households actually paid, how much they spent, and how much they held back.
